def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import glob
    import pandas as pd

    paths = [
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2002.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2003.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2004.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2005.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2006.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2007.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2008.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2009.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2010.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2011.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2012.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2013.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2014.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2015.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2016.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2017.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2018.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2019.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2020.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2021.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2022.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2023.csv",
    ]

    all_files = []
    for p in paths:
        matches = glob.glob(p)
        if not matches:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"No files matched: {p}")
        all_files.extend(matches)

    dfs = []
    for fp in sorted(set(all_files)):
        # year from filename
        import re
        m = re.search(r"(20\d{2})", fp)
        year = int(m.group(1)) if m else None
        df = pd.read_csv(fp)
        df["sourceFile"] = fp
        df["year"] = year
        dfs.append(df)

    out = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True, sort=False)
    return out

operators.customDisplayName: Load and concatenate annual water-body testing CSVs for years 2002-2023 inclusive from provided file paths (using glob for each path); add provenance columns 'sourceFile' (file path) and 'year' (parsed 4-digit year from filename); return combined table (no row subsetting).

def process(loadAllYears) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = loadAllYears
    cols = list(df.columns)
    sample = df.head(5)

    # simple non-null counts for top columns
    nn = df.notna().sum().sort_values(ascending=False).head(40)
    nn_df = nn.reset_index()
    nn_df.columns = ["column", "nonNullCount"]

    # return columns list and sample as a compact table
    cols_df = pd.DataFrame({"column": cols})
    cols_df["order"] = range(len(cols_df))

    # combine: first rows show sample columns and values? keep separate blocks via concat with markers
    sample_long = sample.reset_index(drop=True).melt(var_name="column", value_name="sampleValue")
    sample_long = sample_long.groupby("column").head(1)

    out = cols_df.merge(nn_df, on="column", how="left").merge(sample_long, on="column", how="left")
    out = out.sort_values("order").drop(columns=["order"])
    return out

operators.customDisplayName: Inspect combined dataset schema: list all columns in loadAllYears in original order, along with non-null counts (overall) and a representative sample value from the first 5 rows for each column (to identify key fields like beach name, water-body type, and violation indicator).

Compute count of marine beaches that had zero violations across all observed records from 2002-2023 (missing years assumed safe): detect columns for beach name, water type (filter rows containing 'marine'), and violation indicator (column name contains 'violation' or related terms); flag a record as violation via boolean/numeric truthiness or string token matching; group by beach name and mark anyViolation=any(record violation); return safeMarineBeachesAllYears as integer plus chosen column names for transparency.
